name: C++20 Open-World Game Engine
description: Build a C++20 single-player 3D open-world engine from scratch with a standalone runtime and editor for Windows x64 (DX12/Vulkan) and Linux x64 (Vulkan), in-house ECS/windowing/input, fully vendored offline dependencies, and all mandatory rendering, world, gameplay, editor, packaging, and RTX 5080 acceptance features. Source of truth: tasks/prd-open-world-engine.md; read its applicable global requirements, dependency catalog, image profiles, workload tables, and Performance Contract for each story. These tasks describe future implementation and do not claim successful builds or measurements.

userStories.title: CMake and Initial Checks
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a reproducible build so that I can begin implementation on both operating systems.
acceptanceCriteria: Add the root `CMakeLists.txt`, the presets defined in Quality Gates, isolated build directories, and C++20 without compiler extensions for first-party code.
Create minimal `engine_core`, `engine_runtime`, and `engine_tests` targets; include Catch2 sources in `third_party/` with its license and manifest entry.
Implement `ValidateVendor.cmake`, the initial manifest, and real CLI tests for help, unknown arguments, and nonzero error exit codes.
Configuration performs no network operations; a missing tool or vendor file produces a clear error.

userStories.title: Documentation and Final Release
userStories.description: As an engine user, I want a clear, working package so that I can build the engine and release a sample game.
acceptanceCriteria: The README describes OS/SDK requirements, offline CMake setup, the editor workflow, Lua API, asset pipeline, and native packaging.
Add architecture documentation, component/scene schemas, the vendor manifest/notices, benchmark reproduction instructions, and a capability matrix.
A complete acceptance checklist maps mandatory features to tests and artifacts; all standalone packages pass a clean-directory smoke test.

Apply the constraints relevant to this story in tasks/prd-open-world-engine.md, including Functional Requirements, Non-Goals, Technical Considerations, and the fixed benchmark/performance contract; do not replace mandatory deliverables with stubs.
Windows quality gate: cmake -P cmake/ValidateVendor.cmake passes.
Windows quality gate: cmake --preset win-dev passes.
Windows quality gate: cmake --build --preset win-debug passes.
Windows quality gate: ctest --preset win-unit --output-on-failure --no-tests=error passes.
Linux quality gate: cmake -P cmake/ValidateVendor.cmake passes.
Linux quality gate: cmake --preset linux-dev passes.
Linux quality gate: cmake --build --preset linux-debug passes.
Linux quality gate: ctest --preset linux-unit --output-on-failure --no-tests=error passes.

Apply common checks available at this implementation stage: US-001 establishes verification infrastructure, and US-002 through US-004 extend dependencies, shader tools, and CI. Complete this story against its own deliverables without waiting for future dependent stories.

CTest win-unit/linux-unit include CPU tests labeled unit or integration with functional coverage; an empty smoke test alone is insufficient. First-party code compiles with warnings treated as errors; vendor code does not inherit that requirement.

Once established in US-004, CI builds Windows/MSVC and Linux/Clang for every story; do not report an operating system as verified until its job succeeds. The separate Linux/GCC CI job passes cmake --preset linux-gcc, cmake --build --preset linux-gcc-debug, and ctest --preset linux-gcc-unit --output-on-failure --no-tests=error.

For changes involving memory, ECS, jobs, streaming, Lua, or physics, pass cmake --preset linux-asan, cmake --build --preset linux-asan, and ctest --preset linux-sanitize --output-on-failure --no-tests=error with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer enabled for CPU tests.
Report unavailable GPU extensions or GUI checks as unsupported/not-run rather than passed; WSL and software rendering do not replace required Windows and native Linux GPU reports.

For changes affecting performance, once the benchmark harness and relevant workloads exist, run engine_bench --suite acceptance --backend <dx12|vulkan> --output artifacts/bench/<run-id> using the applicable native OS/backend combinations. Measure in Release without debug/validation overhead; do not require the full suite for documentation-only changes.

Once the corresponding GPU subsystems exist, engine_tests --suite gpu --backend dx12 passes on Windows, and engine_tests --suite gpu --backend vulkan passes on Windows and native Linux. Debug runs enable the D3D12 debug layer or Vulkan validation layers; lifetime, synchronization, resource-state, and GPU validation errors fail the check. Record unimplemented backends at early stages without claiming cross-backend readiness.

Once the corresponding editor test infrastructure exists, engine_tests --suite editor --backend <dx12|vulkan> passes for the available supported native OS/backend combinations, covering the editor scenarios relevant to this story.

Verify UI behavior in the running native application whenever the environment permits, retaining screenshots, an action sequence, and a result log. If no GUI is available, run applicable automated editor-model, serialization, and command checks and document the limitation; these checks do not establish visual readiness.

Final acceptance requires actual GPU reports for Windows/DX12, Windows/Vulkan, and native Linux/Vulkan on the reference RTX 5080 computer, and visual editor smoke tests on both operating systems; unavailable environments leave final acceptance incomplete.

Final release quality gates: cmake --build --preset win-release and cmake --build --preset linux-release pass on their native operating systems; verify an offline build from a clean repository copy, standalone packages from clean directories, and the full performance acceptance suite. Every mandatory feature maps to tests or verifiable artifacts; missing features, platforms, or reports retain incomplete status.
